Shared-format accessors for multiGGMr fits

Source: R/ggmtools-methods.R
multiggm-accessors.Rd

Methods for the ggmtools generics ggmtools::pip_table() and ggmtools::pcor_estimate(), so that downstream code written for those generics works on multiGGMr fits as well as on fits from other packages (e.g. spikeyglass).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'multiggm_fit'
pip_table(fit, varnames = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiggm_fit_list'
pip_table(fit, chain = NULL, varnames = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiggm_platform_fit'
pip_table(fit, platform, varnames = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiggm_fit'
pcor_estimate(fit, varnames = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiggm_fit_list'
pcor_estimate(fit, chain = NULL, varnames = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiggm_platform_fit'
pcor_estimate(fit, platform, varnames = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit, multiggm_fit_list or multiggm_platform_fit.

varnames

Optional variable names.

...

Ignored.

chain

For a multiggm_fit_list: NULL (default) pools all chains; an integer selects chains.

platform

Platform to use for a multiggm_platform_fit.

Value

pip_table(): a data frame with columns i, j, node1, node2, group, pip. pcor_estimate(): a list of K partial-correlation matrices named Group_1, ..., Group_K.

Details

pip_table() returns each group's own posterior edge-inclusion probabilities (from pip_edges()) in long format. It needs edge indicators, so it stops for mGHS fits. pcor_estimate() returns the posterior mean partial correlations (as fitted()). For multi-chain fits all chains are pooled unless chain selects one, as for pip_edges(); for multi-platform fits, choose platform.

multiGGMr fits do not store variable names, so the nodes are labelled V1, ..., Vp unless varnames is given.

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, burnin = 100, nsave = 50)
head(pip_table(fit))
#>   i j node1 node2   group  pip
#> 1 1 2    V1    V2 Group_1 0.46
#> 2 1 3    V1    V3 Group_1 0.98
#> 3 2 3    V2    V3 Group_1 1.00
#> 4 1 4    V1    V4 Group_1 0.00
#> 5 2 4    V2    V4 Group_1 0.66
#> 6 3 4    V3    V4 Group_1 0.30
pcor_estimate(fit)$Group_1[1:3, 1:3]
#>             V1          V2         V3
#> V1  1.00000000 -0.06305474 -0.2820263
#> V2 -0.06305474  1.00000000  0.3031916
#> V3 -0.28202632  0.30319164  1.0000000
